summary: BBN's report on ARPANET host status for November 8 to 19, 1971. It lists hosts that were excluded from the daily tests and notes changes, such as hosts becoming servers or users. It was replaced by RFC 287.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 267 records ARPANET host checks from November 8 to November 19, 1971, and notes which hosts were excluded from testing. During the period, Lincoln's TX2 became a user and SDC's IBM 360/67 became a server; RFC 287 later replaced this report.

subtitle: A November 1971 report of host tests and changes in host roles

tldr.problem: Network operators needed a record of host accessibility and which hosts were ready to serve other sites.
tldr.mechanism: The report lists daily test outcomes, hosts omitted from testing, and operator predictions about server status.
tldr.outcome: It records the TX2 at Lincoln becoming a network user and the SDC IBM 360/67 becoming a server; RFC 287 later replaced it.

sections.title: Reporting Period and Exclusions
sections.content:
The report covers most Network Hosts from November 8 through November 19. The BBN prototype Terminal IMP was inaccessible on November 18 because of hardware debugging.

Some hosts were excluded from daily tests because they were not expected to operate as servers for at least two weeks. Other hosts were intended only as users. The report lists the hosts in each category.
sections.plainLanguage: The report covers most hosts for the listed period, but not every host was tested. Some were not expected to serve other sites soon, and some were user-only machines.

sections.title: Daily Test Results
sections.content:
Two tables show the date and Eastern time of each test, the host's site and computer, and the result. O means the host opened a connection and was accessible to users; D means it was dead or inaccessible from the BBN Terminal IMP; T means it did not respond, although it was not dead.

R means the host refused the initial request. H means the host opened a connection but then closed it or stopped responding. A separate mark identifies sites that warned they might not be available at those times.
sections.plainLanguage: The tables use letters to summarize each test. They distinguish a working connection from no response, refusal, partial response, or inaccessibility.

sections.title: Host Roles and Predictions
sections.content:
The report says that the Lincoln Labs TX2 became a network user during these two weeks, while the SDC IBM 360/67 was now a server. A separate table gives reported server status or expected timing for hosts and names the person who provided each prediction.

The document is a time-specific status report. RFC 287 is listed in the unit metadata as the RFC that later obsoleted it.
sections.plainLanguage: The report notes two role changes and lists operator estimates about other machines. Each test result describes only the date shown in the table.

references.text: Wentheimer, E., "Network host status," RFC 255, October 1971.
